boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named Rapid City destinations in the practical off-campus orbit, each tied to a specific corridor.

cards.title: Dinosaur Park
cards.subtitle: Skyline Drive corridor
cards.notes: Follow Skyline Drive to the public park and walk the route among its seven concrete dinosaur replicas; use the site signs to identify what you are seeing.
cards.short_summary: A hilltop public park with seven historic dinosaur sculptures.
cards.evidence_claim: Dinosaur Park at 940 Skyline Drive has seven life-size concrete dinosaur replicas and is free to visit.
cards.source_title: Dinosaur Park Gift Shop & Visitors Center
cards.access_notes: The park is at 940 Skyline Drive; the visitor center and shop are separate amenities.

cards.title: Skyline Wilderness Area
cards.subtitle: Skyline Drive corridor
cards.notes: Start from the Skyline Drive trail area and choose a marked hiking or biking route; stay on established trails and bring water for the exposed terrain.
cards.short_summary: City wilderness trails beside the Dinosaur Park area.
cards.evidence_claim: Skyline Wilderness Area is a city park at 2215 Skyline Drive, and the city identifies it as a wilderness area.
cards.access_notes: Use the city-listed Skyline Drive location; trail conditions and weather can affect a visit.

cards.title: Hanson-Larsen Memorial Park
cards.subtitle: West Omaha Street corridor
cards.notes: Use the West Omaha Street approach for the M Hill trail system, then select a route suited to your group’s experience and the conditions that day.
cards.short_summary: A public-access trail network on Rapid City's western edge.
cards.evidence_claim: Hanson-Larsen Memorial Park at 1510 W. Omaha Street has more than 20 miles of trails and is open to the public.
cards.access_notes: The source describes the privately owned park as open to the public; routes include hiking, biking, and bouldering terrain.

cards.title: Wilson Park
cards.subtitle: Mount Rushmore Road corridor
cards.notes: Use the green space for a picnic or a walk, and check the city or event organizer before planning around a seasonal program or winter ice surface.
cards.short_summary: A city park on Mount Rushmore Road with seasonal community uses.
cards.evidence_claim: Wilson Park is located at 1701 Mt. Rushmore Road; the visitor bureau describes seasonal events and winter free ice skating there.
cards.access_notes: City parks listing gives the address; seasonal amenities are not guaranteed daily.

cards.title: West Boulevard Historic District
cards.subtitle: West Boulevard corridor
cards.notes: Walk the public boulevard and observe the district’s late-19th- and early-20th-century residential architecture from the sidewalk; respect private homes and yards.
cards.short_summary: A free historic residential streetscape near downtown.
cards.evidence_claim: The West Boulevard Historic District is near downtown and its buildings represent late-19th- and early-20th-century architectural styles; visiting is listed as free.
cards.access_notes: View the historic homes only from public rights-of-way.

cards.title: The Journey Museum
cards.subtitle: New York Street corridor
cards.notes: Plan a museum visit around the current schedule, then move through the galleries in chronological order to connect regional geology, archaeology, and history.
cards.short_summary: A museum presenting layered Black Hills and Rapid City histories.
cards.evidence_claim: The Journey Museum is at 222 New York Street and presents 2.5 billion years of Black Hills history through geology, paleontology, archaeology, and cultural-history exhibits.
cards.access_notes: The museum's official contact page lists summer hours: Tuesday–Saturday 10 a.m.–5 p.m. and Sunday 1–5 p.m.; verify before going.

cards.title: Memorial Park
cards.subtitle: Eighth Street and Omaha Street corridor
cards.notes: Walk through the park’s memorial features, including the flood memorial, veterans memorial, and Berlin Wall segment; follow posted rules during events.
cards.short_summary: A downtown-edge park with memorials and a Berlin Wall segment.
cards.evidence_claim: Memorial Park is at Eighth and Omaha Streets and includes 1972 Rapid City Flood and veterans memorials plus a piece of the Berlin Wall.
cards.access_notes: The city lists the park at 8th and Omaha Street; memorial features are outdoors.

cards.title: Dahl Arts Center
cards.subtitle: Seventh Street corridor
cards.notes: Visit the galleries at 713 Seventh Street and check the current exhibition calendar before you go; gallery admission is always free, while programs can vary.
cards.short_summary: A downtown arts center with free gallery admission.
cards.evidence_claim: The Dahl Arts Center is at 713 7th Street, has five visual-art galleries, and states that admission is always free with a suggested donation.
cards.access_notes: The Dahl lists Monday–Saturday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m.; some classes and performances may be ticketed.

cards.title: Art Alley
cards.subtitle: Sixth–Seventh Street corridor, between Main and Saint Joseph
cards.notes: Enter the working alley from the downtown street grid and photograph the changing murals without blocking deliveries, doors, or service traffic.
cards.short_summary: An evolving outdoor mural corridor in downtown Rapid City.
cards.evidence_claim: Art Alley is a free, family-friendly community gallery between 6th and 7th Streets and Main and Saint Joseph Streets, with changing wall art.
cards.access_notes: It remains a functioning alley; give vehicles and businesses clear access.

cards.title: City of Presidents
cards.subtitle: Main Street downtown corridor
cards.notes: Use the free mobile or dial-in guide to locate the downtown presidential statues, then choose a section of the route that fits your available walking time.
cards.short_summary: A self-guided downtown route of presidential statues.
cards.evidence_claim: The City of Presidents offers a free mobile tour with an interactive map, statue directory, and audio narration, plus a free dial-in option.
cards.access_notes: The statues are distributed across downtown; the visitor center offers printed guides during its seasonal operation.
